# Style Reference Guide — Zoo Animal Manager (Digiata brand)

Companion to `generated-docs/specs/design-tokens.css`. Covers what CSS custom properties can't
express on their own. All hex values below are defined once in `design-tokens.css` — nothing here
introduces a new colour; this document only explains how and when to reach for each token.

Brand source: live-site harvest from `https://www.digiata.com/`, recorded in `project.md` §Styling &
Branding on 2026-07-29. Theme is **dark-first** — dark is the primary/default theme for this app; light
is a secondary nice-to-have, not an acceptance criterion for any story.

---

## 0. Dark-first default — action required outside this file

`globals.css` defines both `:root` (light) and `.dark` (dark, primary) per
`.claude/policies/styling-centralisation.md` rule 5 ("every colour token has a `:root` value AND a
`.dark` value"). But CSS alone cannot decide *which* one renders by default — that is controlled by
whether the `dark` class is present on the `<html>` element.

**`web/src/app/layout.tsx` currently renders `<html lang="en">` with no theme class**, which means the
browser would render the secondary **light** theme by default — the opposite of what this brand
requires. Whoever builds the app shell (Layer 2, R7) must set:

```tsx
<html lang="en" className="dark">
```

Until that line lands, every verified contrast ratio in this document (all measured against `#090909`)
is inactive and the app renders the untested light palette instead.

---

## 1. Typography

- **Font families:** `font-primary` (Inter, substitutes Sequel Sans Book Disp) is the default body/UI
  font; `font-secondary` (Space Grotesk, substitutes Roobert) is for headings/display only;
  `font-mono` (Roboto Mono) is an exact match, used for anything code-like or tabular-numeric (e.g. an
  `Id` or a raw error message). Apply the body default once, at the `body` selector in
  `@layer base`, not per-component.
- **Weights: 400 and 500 ONLY.** The brand uses no bold anywhere (no 600/700). Emphasis comes from
  size, colour, and weight 500 — never `font-bold`/`font-semibold`. Treat any `font-bold` you're
  tempted to add as a signal to reach for a larger size or `text-foreground` instead.
- **Letter-spacing:** `tracking-tight` is overridden to the brand's `-0.03em` (a signature part of the
  look). Apply it to headings and display text only — never to body copy, which should read at normal
  tracking.
- **In-app scale — use the smaller end.** This is a dense data-CRUD tool, not a marketing site.
  `--text-display` (10rem) and `--text-h1` (4rem) are marketing-page scale and are very unlikely to
  appear anywhere in this app. Prefer:
  - Page/section titles → `text-h3` (2rem) or `text-h4` (1.125rem)
  - Card/dialog titles → `text-h4` (1.125rem)
  - Body copy, table cells, form labels → `text-body` (1rem)
  - Emphasised body copy (e.g. a summary line) → `text-body-md` (1.125rem)
  - Reserve `text-h1`/`text-h2`/`text-display` for a landing/empty-state hero, if one is ever built —
    none is planned in this epic.

## 2. Spacing

Tailwind's default spacing scale (base unit `0.25rem`, unchanged in this project) already lands
exactly on the brand's named steps at these existing utility numbers — no new spacing tokens or
utility classes are needed, only this mapping:

| Brand token | Value | Equivalent Tailwind utility (at `0.25rem` base) |
|---|---|---|
| `--space-1` | 1rem | `p-4` / `gap-4` / `m-4` |
| `--space-1-5` | 1.5rem | `p-6` / `gap-6` / `m-6` |
| `--space-2` | 2rem | `p-8` / `gap-8` / `m-8` |
| `--space-2-5` | 2.5rem | `p-10` / `gap-10` / `m-10` |
| `--space-3` | 3rem | `p-12` / `gap-12` / `m-12` |
| `--space-4` | 4rem | `p-16` / `gap-16` / `m-16` |
| `--space-6` | 6rem | `p-24` / `gap-24` / `m-24` |
| `--space-7` | 7rem | `p-28` / `gap-28` / `m-28` |
| `--grid-gap-main` | 1rem | `gap-4` |

**Guidance for a dense CRUD app:**
- Card padding: `p-6` (1.5rem) — enough breathing room without wasting vertical space in a table-heavy
  UI.
- Section gaps (between list header, filters, and table): `gap-6` (1.5rem) via a `flex flex-col`
  wrapper.
- Form field spacing (label → input → helper/error text, and between fields): `gap-2`/`gap-4`
  (Tailwind's finer sub-brand scale — the brand's own steps start at 1rem and are too coarse for
  field-level rhythm).
- Table row padding: keep to Shadcn `Table`'s own defaults (already tuned for data density); do not
  apply `--space-3`/`--space-4` inside table cells.
- Grid/list gaps at the page level: `gap-4` (`--grid-gap-main`).

## 3. Component Selection

Reach for these Shadcn primitives first (per Critical Rule 1 and the brief's Shadcn CLI list —
`table`, `select`, `skeleton`, `alert`, `form`, `dialog`/`alert-dialog`, alongside the existing
`button`, `card`, `input`, `label`):

| Situation | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| Animal/habitat lists | `Table` | Bare `<div>` grid of rows |
| Habitat picker, habitat filter | `Select` | Native `<select>` styled by hand |
| Loading state (list, detail) | `Skeleton` | Spinner-only or blank screen |
| Failed-to-load / duplicate-name / technical-failure messaging | `Alert` (with `variant` mapped to
  `success`/`warning`/`destructive` tokens below) | Raw coloured `<div>` |
| Delete confirmation | `AlertDialog` (not a bare `Dialog`) — it exists specifically for
  "are you sure, this is destructive" flows and pairs with `--destructive` | A plain `Dialog` styled
  to look like a warning |
| Add/edit animal form | `Form` (Zod-backed, per `web/src/lib/validation/`) inside a `Card` or
  `Dialog`, shared between add and edit (R21) | Two near-duplicate forms |
| Animal detail view | `Card` with labelled field rows | An unstyled definition list |
| Toasts (write confirmations/errors) | Existing `ToastContext`/`components/toast/` (NFR-5) | A new
  parallel notification system |

## 4. Layout

- **Max width:** constrain the main content column to a readable width for data tables —
  `max-w-6xl` (~72rem) for the animal/habitat list and detail views, centred with `mx-auto`. Forms
  and dialogs can be narrower (`max-w-xl`/`max-w-2xl`).
- **Breakpoints (per NFR-base-3):** mobile ≥360px, tablet ≥768px, desktop ≥1280px. Use Tailwind's
  `sm:`/`md:`/`lg:` prefixes accordingly.
- **Table responsiveness:** below `md:`, prefer a stacked-card fallback over horizontal-scroll for the
  animal list (five columns — Name, Species, Age, Habitat, Diet — won't fit 360px comfortably);
  horizontal scroll is an acceptable fallback if a stacked layout isn't feasible for a given story.
- **Grid gap:** use `--grid-gap-main` (`gap-4`) for any CSS grid/flex layout at the page or card-grid
  level.
- **App shell:** a single `<main>` landmark (per R7's accessibility note — `layout.tsx` currently
  nests one `<main>` inside `ToastProvider` and `page.tsx` renders a second; the replacement shell
  must resolve to exactly one).

## 5. Motion & Animation

- Existing `modalEnter`/`modalExit`/`slideInFromRight`/`slideOutToRight` keyframes and the
  `prefers-reduced-motion` media query in `globals.css` are preserved as-is — reuse them for the
  `AlertDialog`/`Dialog` and toast transitions rather than introducing new keyframes.
- Keep transitions short and purposeful (150–250ms) — this is a functional tool, not a marketing
  site; avoid decorative motion on table rows or list items.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for anything new: guard any additional custom animation the same
  way the existing keyframes are guarded.

## 6. Accessibility

- **Contrast minimums:** WCAG 2.1 AA baseline (NFR-base-1) — 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large
  text (≥24px or ≥19px bold — though this brand never uses bold, so treat large text as ≥24px
  regular weight) and for non-text UI (borders, icons, focus indicators).
- **Verified pairs (dark theme, primary):**

  | Pair | Ratio | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `--foreground` (#fff9ec) on `--background` (#090909) | 19.0:1 | AAA |
  | `--muted-foreground` (#a8a8a8) on `--background` | 8.4:1 | AAA |
  | `--primary` (#ff6b01) on `--background` (as link/accent text) | 6.9:1 | AA |
  | `--primary-foreground` (#090909) on `--primary` fill | 6.9:1 | AA |
  | `--destructive` (#ff5c5c) on `--background` | ~6.6:1 | AA |
  | `--success` (#7cb342) on `--background` | ~8.0:1 | AAA |
  | `--warning` (#c9a227) on `--background` | ~8.2:1 | AAA |

- **Hard rule — never carry the dark-theme orange onto a light surface.** `#ff6b01` on `#fff9ec`
  measures 2.7:1 and fails AA for any text size. If a light card, printable view, or light theme is
  ever built, use `--color-brand-primary-dark` (`#ad4800`, already wired as `:root`'s `--primary`) for
  any orange text/icon — never the full-brightness accent.
- **Focus ring visibility:** `--ring` is tied to the brand accent (`#ff6b01` dark / `#ad4800` light)
  specifically so focus indicators stay on-brand while remaining well above the 3:1 non-text minimum.
  Don't override `focus-visible:ring-*` per component — the Shadcn primitives already read `--ring`.
- **Keyboard navigation:** every interactive control must be reachable and operable via keyboard
  alone — `Table` row actions, `Select` (habitat picker/filter), and `AlertDialog` confirm/cancel all
  need visible focus states (inherited from `--ring` automatically via Shadcn) and must not rely on
  hover-only affordances (e.g. a delete icon that only appears on `:hover` with no keyboard-reachable
  equivalent).

## 7. Brand Tone

- **Microcopy:** direct and factual, not playful — this is an internal back-office tool with a single
  user type, not a consumer product. "Animal saved" rather than "Great job, animal saved!"
- **Error tone:** per R20/R24, surface the backend's own message where it exists (duplicate-name
  warning, success confirmation) rather than inventing wording; for technical failures, translate the
  raw backend/database message into one readable sentence rather than either suppressing it or
  dumping it verbatim (Critical Rule 3 / NFR-base-6).
- **Warning vs error, visually and verbally distinct:** a duplicate-name rejection is a business rule
  (`--warning`, "This name is already in use — try another"), not a system failure (`--destructive`,
  "Something went wrong saving this animal — your changes are still here, try again"). Never render
  both with the same `Alert` variant.
- **Button labels:** verb-first and specific — "Save animal", "Delete animal", "Add animal" — not bare
  "Submit"/"OK", especially for the destructive path where R22 requires the confirmation to name the
  animal being removed and state the action is irreversible.
- **Never present `LastChangedUser` as attribution** (BR14) — label it as a system/audit trail
  ("Last updated") rather than "Edited by", since every record shows the same fixed deployment value.

## Status colour rationale (BUILD decision — not harvested)

Digiata's palette is single-accent orange; this app needs success/warning/destructive states the
brand site has no equivalent for. Each was chosen to (a) sit harmoniously with the warm neutral ramp
rather than reading as a cold, clinical hue, (b) hit ≥4.5:1 on `#090909`, and (c) stay clearly distinct
in hue from the brand orange (~25°) so "primary action" and "destructive action" can never be confused
(NFR-4):

| Role | Hex (dark) | Hue | Contrast on `#090909` | Distinct from orange (~25°) by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Destructive | `#ff5c5c` | ~0° | ~6.6:1 (AA) | 25° hue separation, and a true-red profile (high blue channel) rather than orange's near-zero blue |
| Success | `#7cb342` | ~90° | ~8.0:1 (AAA) | opposite side of the colour wheel — green, unambiguous |
| Warning | `#c9a227` | ~46° | ~8.2:1 (AAA) | lower saturation, more yellow, and a much higher blue channel than orange — reads as gold/mustard, not orange |

Light-theme variants (`#c93a3e` destructive, `#4d7c22` success, `#8a6d1a` warning) are deliberately
darker than their dark-theme counterparts, since they sit on the light `#fff9ec` background instead of
`#090909` — each still clears 4.5:1 AA (measured 4.7–4.8:1; see `design-tokens.css` comments for exact
figures).
